Developing pbtm

Source: DEVELOPMENT.md

Notes for maintainers: the day-to-day workflow, and how to cut a release, tag it on GitHub, submit it to CRAN, and publish the pkgdown site. This file is excluded from the package build (.Rbuildignore).

Setup

install.packages(c("devtools", "usethis", "roxygen2", "testthat", "pkgdown",
                   "rcmdcheck", "spelling", "urlchecker"))
devtools::install_dev_deps()   # everything in Imports and Suggests

To use the GitHub helpers in usethis (releases, PRs), you need a GitHub personal access token: usethis::create_github_token(), then gitcreds::gitcreds_set(). Check with usethis::gh_token_help().

Day to day

Task Command
Load the package for interactive use devtools::load_all()
Regenerate man/ and NAMESPACE from roxygen comments devtools::document()
Run the tests devtools::test()
Full check, as CI runs it devtools::check()
Spell check (add real words to inst/WORDLIST) spelling::spell_check_package()
Preview the website pkgdown::build_site() (writes to docs/, which is git-ignored)
Rebuild the example datasets from data-raw/*.csv source("data-raw/datasets.R") (needs readr)

Never edit man/*.Rd or NAMESPACE by hand; they are generated by roxygen2.

Work on a feature branch and open a pull request into main. The R-CMD-check workflow runs R CMD check on Windows, macOS, and Linux for every push and pull request, and the pkgdown workflow test-builds the site. Merge only when both are green.

Most of the tests run everywhere, but the mixture-fitting tests and the fresh-session namespace test call skip_on_cran(). They run in CI and under devtools::test()/devtools::check() (which set NOT_CRAN=true), but not on CRAN’s machines, because they are slow.

Versions

pbtm uses semantic versioning: major.minor.patch.

  • patch (0.3.0 → 0.3.1): bug fixes only.
  • minor (0.3.0 → 0.4.0): new features, or breaking changes while the package is below 1.0.0.
  • major (→ 1.0.0): the API is stable; from then on, breaking changes bump the major version.

Between releases, main carries a development version with a fourth component, e.g. 0.3.0.9000. Add a bullet to the top section of NEWS.md (headed # pbtm (development version)) for every user-facing change as you make it, so the release notes are already written at release time.

usethis::use_version() bumps DESCRIPTION and NEWS.md together: use_version("patch"), "minor", "major", or "dev".

Releasing

A release is: bump the version, check thoroughly, submit to CRAN, and once CRAN accepts it, tag the release on GitHub. The GitHub release triggers a rebuild of the website.

The easiest way to not miss a step is to run usethis::use_release_issue(), which opens a GitHub issue with a checklist tailored to this package. The steps it lists are summarized here.

1. Prepare

On main (or a release branch merged via PR), with a clean working tree:

usethis::use_version("minor")   # or "patch" / "major"; drops the .9000

Then edit NEWS.md: change the heading to the new version and tidy the bullets. Also check:

  • README.md is current (e.g. the installation instructions once on CRAN).
  • urlchecker::url_check() finds no broken links (CRAN rejects them).
  • spelling::spell_check_package() is clean.

2. Check

CRAN runs R CMD check --as-cran on several platforms, so check on those platforms before submitting. All of these should report 0 errors and 0 warnings; any NOTEs must be explained in cran-comments.md.

devtools::check(remote = TRUE, manual = TRUE)  # local, with CRAN's incoming checks
devtools::check_win_devel()                    # Windows, R-devel (results by email, ~30 min)
devtools::check_mac_release()                  # macOS (results by email)
rhub::rhub_check()                             # Linux sanitizers etc., via GitHub Actions

rhub::rhub_check() runs in this repository’s GitHub Actions; the first time, run rhub::rhub_setup() and commit the workflow file it creates.

The win-builder and mac-builder results are emailed to the maintainer listed in DESCRIPTION, not to whoever ran the command.

R CMD check on a first submission always gives the NOTE “New submission”; that is expected.

3. Submit to CRAN

Create cran-comments.md (once; update it for each release) with usethis::use_cran_comments(). It summarizes the check results and explains any NOTEs. For example:

## R CMD check results

0 errors | 0 warnings | 1 note

* This is a new release.

Then submit:

devtools::submit_cran()

This builds the package, uploads it, and writes a CRAN-SUBMISSION file recording the commit that was submitted. CRAN then emails the maintainer (Pedro Bello) a link that must be clicked to confirm the submission. Commit CRAN-SUBMISSION and cran-comments.md.

CRAN review takes from a day to a few weeks. First submissions are reviewed by a person and often come back with requests (e.g. about the Description text, examples, or writing to the user’s home directory). Fix them, bump the patch version if needed, and resubmit, noting the changes in cran-comments.md.

CRAN policy: don’t submit updates more often than about every 1-2 months.

4. Tag and publish the GitHub release

Once CRAN accepts the package (you’ll get an email, and it appears at https://cran.r-project.org/package=pbtm), tag the release:

usethis::use_github_release()

This creates the vX.Y.Z git tag on the commit recorded in CRAN-SUBMISSION (so the tag matches exactly what CRAN has), publishes a GitHub release with the NEWS.md section as its notes, and deletes CRAN-SUBMISSION. Publishing the release triggers the pkgdown workflow, which rebuilds the site.

To do it by hand instead:

git tag -a v0.3.0 -m "pbtm 0.3.0"
git push origin v0.3.0

then on GitHub, Releases → Draft a new release, choose the tag, and paste the NEWS.md section as the description.

5. Start the next development cycle

usethis::use_dev_version(push = TRUE)   # 0.3.0 -> 0.3.0.9000, adds NEWS heading

GitHub-only releases

To publish a version without submitting to CRAN (e.g. before the first CRAN release), follow steps 1-2, merge to main, then run step 4 (usethis::use_github_release() falls back to the current HEAD of main when there is no CRAN-SUBMISSION file). Users can then install that exact version with remotes::install_github("pbt-models/pbtm@v0.3.0").

Website (pkgdown)

The site at https://pbt-models.github.io/pbtm/ is built by .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml on every push to main and every published release, and deployed to the gh-pages branch. It is configured in _pkgdown.yml:

  • The Reference page groups the help topics. Every exported function must be listed there, so when you add one, add it to a section (or the site build fails). pkgdown::check_pkgdown() checks this.
  • The Get started article is vignettes/pbtm.Rmd; the other vignettes are listed under Models. Add new vignettes to the articles section.
  • The changelog is built from NEWS.md.

One-time setup (repository admin): after the workflow has run once on main and created the gh-pages branch, go to Settings → Pages and set Source to Deploy from a branch, branch gh-pages, folder / (root). Then add the site URL to the repository’s About box on GitHub.
